model.name: Dependency / Impact
model.purpose: Provide a format-neutral mixin that lets any host subject declare typed dependency conditions on prerequisites, with explicit strength, conditionality, exclusion and satisfaction-state semantics, so that an agent can read, author and interoperably project a dependency declaration without resolving, evaluating or enforcing it.
model.scope_statement: This bounded pass covers the declaration surface of a dependency condition and the epistemic state attached to it. A dependency condition is an addressable, attributed assertion that a dependent subject requires, prefers, precedes or excludes some prerequisite target, optionally under a guard, within a lifecycle scope, and against a comparison predicate or range. The mixin is applied to host entities that it does not define; it fixes the canonical dependent-to-prerequisite direction, the neutral strength and obligation vocabulary, the logical form of alternatives, guards, thresholds and negative conditions, and the separation between a declared condition and any observed satisfaction, violation, deviation or unknown state. Storage and interface (JSON, YAML, Markdown, Git, MCP, MongoDB) are projections of this semantics, never its definition.
in_scope: Identity of an individual dependency condition, independent of the entities it connects
Canonical dependent-to-prerequisite direction and normalization of reverse-declared or prerequisite-side forms
Typed dependency kind and lifecycle or phase scope of the condition
Strength, obligation level, optionality encoding and declared preference weight
Ordered prerequisites, the required state of the prerequisite at a stage boundary, and the orthogonality of ordering to existence requirements
Alternative sets, cardinality bounds, n-of-m satisfaction thresholds and same-target binding
Guards and applicability predicates, including the distinction between inapplicable and failed
Comparison predicates, compatibility and version ranges, interval inclusivity and quantitative thresholds
Negative conditions, declared incompatibilities and mutually contradictory declarations
Recorded satisfaction, violation, not-applicable, unknown and deviation state as references and snapshots
Completeness and no-assertion disclosure over a scoped set of declarations, and the open-world default
out_of_scope: Impact propagation, blast radius, downstream effect and criticality scoring, which belong to the impact split of this model
Dependency resolution, constraint solving, package selection, scheduling and installation ordering execution
Evaluation of guards, predicates or ranges, and any re-evaluation trigger, cache or scheduler owned by an external evaluator
Policy enforcement, gating decisions, admission control and remediation actions
Ownership of the evaluator's or authority's audit trail, evidence retention and non-repudiation machinery
Approval workflow, delegation and authority verification behind a waiver, concession or exception
Graph analytics such as transitive closure, cycle detection, topological sorting and shortest-path attribution
Identity, versioning and precedence rules for the prerequisite targets themselves, including version ordering schemes
Vulnerability, licence and provenance assertions about the prerequisite, which are separate cross-cutting models
Discovery, scanning or inference of undeclared dependencies from artefacts or telemetry

boundary_notes.neighbor: Impact propagation and criticality split of WM-XCT-037
boundary_notes.distinction: This pass stops at the declared condition and its recorded state. Whether an unmet or violated condition propagates, how far, and with what severity to the dependent's own function is impact semantics and is deliberately not modelled here; only the declared, non-binding consequence note supplied by the source vocabulary is carried.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Dependency resolver, solver, scheduler or package manager
boundary_notes.distinction: Sources that define dependency grammars separate the declaration from the tool that satisfies it: TOSCA requirements are fulfilled by a TOSCA processor at deployment time, and Debian relationship fields are interpreted by dpkg and by autobuilders. This model owns the declaration and its crosswalk; selection among alternatives, resolution of dangling requirements and installation ordering execution belong to the resolver.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Constraint validation processor and validation report
boundary_notes.distinction: SHACL separates a declarative shapes graph from a validation report produced by an external processor. By the same separation, this model carries declared predicates and a reference to an externally produced conformance result; it does not define validation algorithms, report structure or report retention.

A reference to a runtime evaluator or enforcement point conveys only the binding and subject-specific parameters. Evaluation semantics, enforcement outcomes, admission decisions and the engine's audit trail remain owned by that engine's model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Authority and decision-record model for waivers, concessions and exceptions
boundary_notes.distinction: This model records that a deviation exists, its subject binding and its declared validity window, following the requirement-level convention that a departure from a recommended item must have its implications understood and weighed. Who may approve, how approval is evidenced, and how the decision record is retained belong to the authority model.

Ranges are only meaningful under a declared ordering scheme; OSV distinguishes SEMVER precedence, uninterpreted ECOSYSTEM strings and GIT commit-graph ranges. This model carries the scheme reference and the endpoint operands and never defines version precedence itself.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Host subject model supplying dependent and prerequisite entities
boundary_notes.distinction: As a mixin, this model contributes conditions to entities defined elsewhere. Entity identity, description, classification and lifecycle stay with the host model; only the endpoint reference and any selector used to designate an abstract target are carried here.

SPDX separates containment and optional-component relationships from dependency relationships. A part-of or contains relation is not a dependency condition, and this model does not represent bill-of-materials assembly structure.

sources.title: SPDX Specification 3.0.1 - Core Vocabularies: RelationshipType
sources.relevance: Normative typed dependency vocabulary: dependsOn, hasOptionalDependency, hasProvidedDependency, hasPrerequisite, hasRequirement, hasStaticLink and hasDynamicLink, each defined as from-Element to to-Element and qualified by a lifecycle scope. Establishes strength and provisioning mode as relationship typing and fixes the dependent-to-prerequisite direction.

sources.title: SPDX Specification 3.0.1 - Core Vocabularies: RelationshipCompleteness
sources.relevance: Defines complete, incomplete and noAssertion as explicit statements about whether a declared relationship set is exhaustive, providing normative grounding for open-world completeness disclosure and for an explicit unknown state.

sources.title: SPDX Specification 3.0.1 - Core Vocabularies: LifecycleScopeType
sources.relevance: Enumerates build, design, development, runtime, test and other as scopes that give context to a relationship, because a dependency may be critical in one phase and irrelevant in another. Grounds phase-scoped conditions as distinct from unconditional edges.

sources.title: ECMA-424 CycloneDX Bill of materials specification
sources.relevance: Formal standardisation of the CycloneDX syntax and semantics for describing components, services, dependencies and compositions; used as the standards-body anchor for the dependency-graph representation and its terminology.

sources.title: Inventory Management Use Case: Software Dependencies
sources.relevance: Defines ref and dependsOn against bom-ref identifiers and states the critical epistemic rule that components with no dependencies must be declared as empty elements, while components absent from the graph may have unknown dependencies and must be treated as opaque rather than dependency-free.

sources.title: Debian Policy Manual - Chapter 7: Declaring relationships between packages
sources.relevance: Graded strength fields (Pre-Depends, Depends, Recommends, Suggests, Enhances), alternative syntax using the pipe operator, version relations (<<, <=, =, >=, >>), architecture and build-profile restrictions in disjunctive normal form, negative relations (Conflicts, Breaks, Replaces), virtual targets via Provides, and staged ordering semantics for Pre-Depends across unpack and configure.

sources.title: RPM Reference Manual - Boolean Dependencies
sources.version_or_date: Documentation for operators introduced in RPM 4.13 and 4.14, accessed 2026-09-04
sources.relevance: Defines and, or, if, if-else, unless, unless-else, with and without, giving normative grammar for alternatives, guarded (conditional) dependencies, negative guards and same-target binding, plus the restriction that if cannot be combined with or and unless cannot be combined with and, and that Provides cannot carry boolean expressions.

sources.title: systemd.unit(5) manual page
sources.organization: systemd project (manual page mirrored by man7.org)
sources.relevance: Distinguishes requirement strength (Requires, Requisite, Wants, BindsTo, PartOf, Upholds), negative requirement (Conflicts) and ordering (Before, After), and states that ordering dependencies are independent of and orthogonal to requirement dependencies. Condition directives cause a silent skip when unmet whereas Assert directives cause failure, which is the canonical inapplicable-versus-failed distinction.

sources.title: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL)
sources.relevance: Separates a declarative shapes graph from a validation report produced by an external processor, defines conformance as absence of results and no reported failure, provides the severity scale (Violation, Warning, Info) and provides sh:deactivated as a declared, reversible suspension of a constraint.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Primer (Second Edition)
sources.relevance: States the open-world assumption explicitly: a fact absent from a database is usually considered false under the closed-world assumption, whereas in an OWL 2 document it may simply be missing but possibly true. Grounds the model's default treatment of undeclared conditions as unknown rather than absent.

sources.title: Assigning Pods to Nodes
sources.relevance: Contrasts requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution (hard: cannot proceed unless the rule is met) with preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution (soft: still proceeds), carrying a weight between 1 and 100 that is summed during scoring, and provides matching operators In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt and Lt, where NotIn and DoesNotExist express negative conditions.

sources.title: TOSCA Version 2.0
sources.relevance: Requirement definitions declare a target capability type, node type, relationship type, node filter and count range; a lower bound of zero makes a requirement optional, and mandatory dangling requirements must be fulfilled by a TOSCA processor at deployment time. Grounds cardinality-encoded optionality, abstract target selection by filter, and the declaration-versus-fulfilment boundary.

sources.title: RFC 2119 / BCP 14 - Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels
sources.relevance: Normative obligation levels: MUST as an absolute requirement, MUST NOT as an absolute prohibition, SHOULD where valid reasons may exist in particular circumstances to ignore an item but the full implications must be understood and carefully weighed, and MAY as truly optional. Provides a domain-neutral strength scale and the normative basis for a justified, recorded deviation.

sources.title: Open Source Vulnerability (OSV) Schema
sources.relevance: Range model with SEMVER, ECOSYSTEM and GIT types, an events array (introduced, fixed, last_affected, limit), half-open interval interpretation, and the requirement for an explicit enumerated versions list where the ecosystem ordering is uninterpreted. Grounds range endpoints, inclusivity and the dependence of ranges on a declared ordering scheme.

bundles.name: Declared Dependency Condition
bundles.description: Everything an agent must know to author or read one dependency condition as declared: what it is, which way it points, how strong it is, when it applies, what may satisfy it, and what it forbids.
bundles.rationale: Every authoritative dependency vocabulary examined separates the act of declaring a relationship from the act of satisfying it: SPDX models a relationship as its own element with a type, completeness and lifecycle scope; TOSCA requirements are declared on a node and fulfilled later by a processor; Debian and RPM declare graded, guarded, alternative and negative relations in package metadata that dpkg or the depsolver later interprets. Grouping the declaration surface into one bundle keeps the mixin usable without any resolver present.

layers.name: Condition Core: Identity, Direction, Type and Scope
layers.description: The header of a dependency condition: its own identifier, the canonical dependent-to-prerequisite orientation, the endpoints or selectors it binds, its typed kind, and the lifecycle phase in which it applies.

findings.name: Condition identity, canonical direction, endpoints, typed kind and lifecycle scope
findings.description: A dependency condition is an addressable assertion in its own right, not a property of either endpoint. Its source endpoint is always the dependent and its target is always the prerequisite, matching the SPDX from-to orientation and the CycloneDX ref-to-dependsOn orientation. Some vocabularies declare from the prerequisite side (Debian Enhances, RPM Supplements and Enhances) or use inverse relationship names, so a recorded normalization step is required before the condition can be read in canonical form. The typed kind additionally carries provisioning meaning that must not be confused with strength: SPDX hasProvidedDependency marks a dependency assumed to be provided rather than distributed, and static versus dynamic linkage is a typing distinction, not a strength distinction. The lifecycle scope (build, design, development, runtime, test, other) bounds where the condition applies at all, and a scope-bounded condition is not an unconditional edge.

artifacts.name: Dependency type and direction crosswalk profile
artifacts.description: A governed, versioned mapping between the model's neutral typed-kind and direction vocabulary and each adopted external vocabulary, recording for every term whether the mapping is exact, broader, narrower or unmapped, and which source terms are prerequisite-side declarations requiring inversion.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative master-system profile identifier from the system of record where one exists; otherwise a governed IRI in the adopting Dimension's namespace; otherwise a UUID or ULID assigned at issue. The profile version is a separate ordered attribute and the publication date is never used as the identifier.

layers.name: Strength, Obligation and Ordering
layers.description: The two independent axes that authoritative vocabularies keep separate: how binding the condition is, and whether it also constrains sequence and prerequisite state at a stage boundary.

findings.name: Obligation level, optionality encoding and preference weight
findings.description: Strength is expressed in at least three incompatible ways across authorities: as a distinct relationship type (SPDX dependsOn versus hasOptionalDependency), as a distinct field with graded meaning (Debian Pre-Depends, Depends, Recommends, Suggests; RPM Requires, Recommends, Suggests), and as a cardinality lower bound of zero (TOSCA count range). Kubernetes adds a fourth encoding in which hard rules block the operation and soft rules carry a weight from 1 to 100 that is summed during scoring. RFC 2119 supplies a domain-neutral three-level scale in which SHOULD explicitly admits justified departure. The model therefore records one normalized obligation level plus the native encoding, and refuses to assert a single total order across scales, because an ordinal field grade and a cardinal scheduling weight are not commensurable.

findings.name: Ordered prerequisites and the ordering-versus-existence distinction
findings.description: Ordering is a separate axis from existence. The systemd unit model states that ordering settings are independent of and orthogonal to requirement dependencies, so a unit can require another without ordering against it, and can order against a unit it does not require. Debian Pre-Depends instead couples the two, requiring the prerequisite to be fully installed before the dependent's installation starts, with staged acceptance criteria that differ between unpack and configure and an explicit prohibition on circular pre-dependencies. Requisite adds a further distinction: the prerequisite must already be in the required state and will not be brought into it as part of satisfying the condition. The model therefore records the ordering assertion, the required prerequisite state, the stage boundary being gated, and whether pre-existence is demanded, without computing any sequence.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Ordering semantics are attributes of a single condition declaration carried inside the host record; there is no separable, independently addressable document here. Any sequence plan, topological order or execution schedule that would be a genuine artifact is produced by a resolver, scheduler or init system that owns execution, so materialising one in this model would import operational semantics that the boundary excludes.

layers.name: Condition Expression: Alternatives, Guards, Predicates and Exclusions
layers.description: The logical form of the condition: what set of targets may satisfy it, under what applicability guard it holds at all, against which comparison predicate or range, and what it forbids.

findings.name: Alternative sets, cardinality bounds and n-of-m satisfaction thresholds
findings.description: A single condition may be satisfiable by any of several targets. Debian expresses this with the pipe operator and treats the listed order as meaningful, with autobuilders discarding architecture-mismatched options and taking the first remaining name. RPM expresses it with or, and adds with, which requires all operands to be satisfied by the same package, and without, which requires a package satisfying the first operand but not the second. TOSCA expresses multiplicity as a count range, so the satisfaction threshold is a bounded interval rather than a boolean. Kubernetes allows several soft rules to contribute weights independently, which is a scored rather than a thresholded form. The model records the member set, the threshold, whether members must bind to the same target, and whether any preference order is normative or conventional.

findings.inline_only_rationale: An alternative set is an internal structure of one condition expression and has no life outside the condition that carries it; it is neither separately addressable nor separately versioned. Externalising it would create a shadow catalogue of candidate targets, which belongs to the host subject and target-registry models rather than to this mixin.

findings.name: Guards, applicability predicates and the inapplicable-versus-failed distinction
findings.description: A guarded condition holds only when its guard is true, and a false guard makes the condition inapplicable rather than unsatisfied. RPM makes this explicit with if, if-else, unless and unless-else, and constrains their combination so that if cannot appear with or and unless cannot appear with and. Debian restricts relationships by architecture in square brackets, with negation, and by build profile in angle brackets interpreted as disjunctive normal form. systemd separates Condition directives, where an unmet condition causes the unit start to be mostly silently skipped without entering a failed state, from Assert directives, where failure is an error. Kubernetes scopes matching to scheduling and ignores it during execution, so guard evaluation timing is itself part of the declaration. The critical compositional rule is that a guarded condition must never be flattened into an unconditional edge in any projection.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A guard is a predicate belonging to exactly one condition and is meaningless when detached from it; keeping it inline is what prevents the guard from being dropped and the condition from silently becoming unconditional. Any evaluated guard outcome is produced by an external evaluator, so no evaluation artifact is claimed here.

findings.name: Comparison predicates, compatibility ranges and quantitative thresholds
findings.description: Conditions are frequently expressed against a value rather than a bare existence test. Debian defines the version relations strictly earlier, earlier or equal, exactly equal, later or equal and strictly later. The OSV schema shows that a range is only interpretable under a declared ordering scheme: semantic-version precedence, uninterpreted ecosystem strings that need an explicit enumerated version list, or a commit graph that must be consulted; and it fixes the half-open reading in which the fixing endpoint is excluded. Kubernetes supplies set and existence operators and warns that its greater-than and less-than comparisons are lexicographic on label values. TOSCA constrains target selection through node filters over property constraints. The model therefore records the operator, the operands, the endpoint inclusivity, the ordering scheme reference and, for quantitative thresholds, the unit and measurement basis; it never performs the comparison.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Predicates and range endpoints are operands of one condition and are carried as reference data alongside a pointer to an externally governed ordering scheme. The ordering scheme itself, and any evaluation of the predicate, are owned by the version-identity model and by the evaluator respectively, so this finding holds only inline operands and references.

findings.name: Negative conditions and declared incompatibilities
findings.description: Not all dependency conditions are positive. Debian defines Conflicts, which prevents two packages from being unpacked simultaneously, and Breaks, which prevents configuration of a broken package while the breaking package is unpacked, alongside Replaces. RPM permits boolean expressions in Conflicts and provides unless and without as negative forms, and states that Provides may not carry boolean expressions. systemd defines Conflicts as a negative requirement in which starting one unit stops the other, and Kubernetes uses NotIn and DoesNotExist to express anti-affinity. A negative condition is therefore a first-class declaration with the same identity, direction, scope and strength machinery as a positive one, and two declarations can be mutually contradictory as authored. This finding records exclusions and asserted contradictions; it does not detect, rank or resolve them.

findings.inline_only_rationale: An exclusion is a condition declaration carried on the host record using the same inline structure as a positive condition, and an asserted contradiction is a typed cross-reference between two such declarations. A consistency or solver report that would justify an artifact is produced and retained by the external checker, and claiming it here would import evaluation and audit semantics the boundary excludes.

bundles.name: Satisfaction State and Epistemic Disclosure
bundles.description: How a declared condition relates to what is actually known: recorded satisfaction, violation, inapplicability, unknown state and deviation, and the completeness of the declaration set as a whole.
bundles.rationale: Every authority examined insists on this separation. SHACL keeps a declarative shapes graph apart from a validation report produced by an external processor and defines conformance as the absence of results with no failure reported. CycloneDX warns that absence from the dependency graph must be treated as opaque rather than as evidence of having no dependencies. SPDX provides complete, incomplete and noAssertion as explicit completeness statements. OWL 2 states the open-world assumption directly. Modelling declaration and knowledge in one undifferentiated structure would convert missing information into false information.

layers.name: Observed Satisfaction, Violation and Deviation
layers.description: The per-condition record of what is known about satisfaction at a point in time, including inapplicability, unknown state and any recorded deviation, all carried as references to externally owned results and decisions.

findings.name: Declared condition versus recorded satisfaction, violation, inapplicability, unknown state and deviation
findings.description: The declared condition and any statement about its satisfaction are different objects with different provenance and different time bases. Following the SHACL separation, this model carries a status snapshot and a reference to the externally produced result, never the evaluation itself: conformance in SHACL is defined as an empty result set with no reported failure, and the report is produced by a processor. The status vocabulary must distinguish satisfied, violated, not-applicable (the guard was false, which systemd treats as a silent skip rather than a failure) and unknown, since silence is not satisfaction. Severity is a declared qualifier of a result, as in the SHACL Violation, Warning and Info scale, and is not the same as the condition's obligation level. A deviation, whether a waiver, a concession or a declared deactivation in the sense of a shape that is switched off while remaining defined, is recorded as a reference to a decision owned elsewhere, together with its subject binding and declared validity window, on the requirement-level principle that departure from a recommended item demands that its implications be understood and weighed.

Declaring an artifact here would amount to owning an evaluation output or an audit trail, which the boundary explicitly assigns elsewhere, so the finding is deliberately reference-only.

layers.name: Completeness, Open-World Assumptions and Assertion Scope
layers.description: Statements about the declaration set as a whole rather than about any single condition: how exhaustive it is, over what scope, and how absence must be read.

findings.name: Completeness assertion, open-world default and the reading of absence
findings.description: A set of declared conditions is not a closed world unless someone says so. SPDX makes this explicit with complete, incomplete and noAssertion, meaning the relationship is known to be exhaustive, known not to be exhaustive, or carries no claim. CycloneDX makes the operational consequence explicit: a component with no dependencies must be declared as an empty element, whereas a component absent from the graph may have unknown dependencies and should be treated as opaque rather than dependency-free. OWL 2 states the underlying epistemics, that a fact absent from a document may simply be missing but possibly true. The model therefore defaults to the open-world reading, requires an explicit empty declaration to assert that a subject genuinely has no conditions of a given kind, and treats completeness as an attributed, scoped assertion with its own provenance rather than as an inferred property.

questions.text: For this subject and scope, is the declared condition set asserted to be exhaustive, non-exhaustive, or is no claim made?

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must designate a named owner for the condition vocabulary, the type and direction crosswalk profile and the strength scale profile, since the registry entry currently records only an unnamed owner designated by the adopting Dimension.

The owner package must publish, before first use, the neutral typed-kind list, obligation-level list, status vocabulary including unknown and not-applicable, polarity list and completeness values, each with a stable term identifier.

The owner package must name, for every referenced external model, which side owns evaluation, resolution, enforcement, approval and retention, and must reject any local field that would duplicate a referenced model's operational semantics.
The owner package must state the default reading of absence for each declaration scope it governs and must default to the open-world reading where no explicit completeness assertion exists.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Terms are minted in a namespace controlled by the adopting Dimension, with a stable path segment for this mixin and separate segments for typed kinds, obligation levels, status values, polarities and completeness values. External vocabulary terms are never minted locally; they are referenced by their owning organisation's identifier and version through the crosswalk profile, and a locally minted term must never reuse an external term's string identity.
registry_links: World-model registry entry vr.wm-xct-037 on the world-model record plane, navigation path NAV.XCT.DEP, domain tag XCT.DEP, review state boundary-review-required
SPDX 3.0.1 term namespace for the relationship-type, relationship-completeness and lifecycle-scope vocabularies as the alignment registry for typed kinds
Ecma International standard register entry for ECMA-424 as the alignment registry for the bill-of-materials dependency-graph projection

canonicalization_rules: Every condition is stored in canonical dependent-to-prerequisite direction; prerequisite-side and inverse-named source forms are inverted on ingest and the native term is retained in the normalization record.

Condition expressions are serialised in a declared normal form with a stable operand order, but normalisation must preserve the original operator structure, because some target grammars forbid operator combinations and a rewritten expression may no longer be projectable.
Timestamps are canonicalised to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, retaining the originally reported offset in provenance where it differs from the storage offset.
Codes are canonicalised to the owner package's term identifiers; unmapped native terms are retained verbatim in the residue list and never coerced to the nearest neutral term.
patch_rules: A change to obligation level, polarity, direction, guard presence or predicate operands creates a new revision of the condition; these fields are never edited in place once any external observation or deviation references the condition.
Withdrawing a guard, widening a lifecycle scope or lowering a satisfaction threshold is a widening change and must be issued as a superseding revision with a stated reason.
Status snapshots, deviation bindings and completeness assertions are append-only; corrections are issued as new records that supersede prior ones by reference rather than by overwrite.
A patch may never convert a guarded or scope-bounded condition into an unconditional one; such a change must be authored as a new, explicitly unconditional condition.
compatibility_rules: Adding a new typed kind, status value or completeness value is backward compatible only if consumers are required to treat unrecognised codes as unknown rather than as a default.
Removing or narrowing an existing typed kind, obligation level or status value is a breaking change and requires a new crosswalk profile major version.
Crosswalk and scale profiles are versioned independently of the condition records that cite them; a condition always cites the profile version under which it was authored.
Numeric preference weights are only comparable within a single named scale version; no cross-scale comparison is compatible, and a projection that implies one is invalid.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record that owns the artifact or condition
Governed global identifier or IRI minted in the adopting Dimension's controlled namespace where no master-system identifier exists
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension as the last resort, recorded together with the assigning process
Native external identifiers, such as a bill-of-materials reference or a package identifier, are retained as cross-references and never promoted to primary identity
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 date-time with explicit seconds and an explicit UTC offset or the literal Z; local times without an offset are rejected on ingest. Event time, meaning when the declaration was authored or the observed state actually changed at source, is recorded separately from observation or ingestion time, meaning when this model received or wrote the record, whenever those differ; neither is derived from the other, and where only one is known the other is left absent rather than copied.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts such as crosswalk profiles, scale profiles and completeness assertions carry an immutable base identifier plus a monotonically increasing version or sequence attribute. The version attribute is ordinal and is never a date, no date component appears in the identifier, and supersession is expressed as an explicit reference from the newer record to the older one.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each serial artifact records a content digest with the named digest algorithm, the issuing actor and the event and observation timestamps. A condition citing a profile version must resolve to that exact digest; if the referenced digest cannot be resolved, the condition is reported as unverifiable rather than assumed valid, and integrity verification of externally owned results and decision records remains the responsibility of the systems that retain them.

policies: Declaration and knowledge are never merged: a condition record states what is required, and any statement about satisfaction is a separately attributed, separately timed record referencing an external producer.

No conditional dependency is ever emitted as an unconditional edge. Any projection that cannot carry a guard, lifecycle scope or alternative structure must be refused or accompanied by a lossiness report naming the dropped distinction.

This model performs no resolution, evaluation, enforcement or execution. It may hold references, subject bindings and validity parameters for externally owned evaluators and authorities, and nothing more.

Absence is read under the open-world assumption by default. A claim that a subject has no conditions of a given kind requires an explicit empty declaration or a completeness assertion, and silence is never treated as evidence of independence.

Alignment to an external standard is recorded as a crosswalk with explicit fidelity classification; conformance is never claimed without evidence, and known conflicts between source vocabularies are recorded rather than reconciled by fiat.

read: Read a condition together with its direction normalization record, guard, scope and the crosswalk profile versions it cites, so that no consumer sees a stripped, unconditional form.
Reads that return a status snapshot must also return its event time, observation time, producing evaluator and any staleness note; a status may not be served without its provenance.
Reads over a scope must return the applicable completeness assertion or, where none exists, an explicit open-world marker.
create: Create a condition only with a resolvable dependent endpoint, a target reference or an explicitly marked selector, a typed kind, an obligation level and a canonical direction marker.
Create status snapshots, deviation bindings and completeness assertions as append-only records that cite the external producer or decision record they depend on.
Reject creation where the requested guard or operator combination is outside the neutral grammar, rather than silently simplifying it.
update: Semantic fields including direction, polarity, obligation level, guard and predicate operands are updated only by issuing a superseding revision that references its predecessor.
Non-semantic corrections such as descriptive notes may be updated in place, with the editing actor and observation time recorded.
Updating a crosswalk or scale profile never retroactively changes conditions authored under an earlier profile version; those conditions keep their cited version.
delete: Conditions are not hard-deleted. A withdrawn condition is marked withdrawn with a withdrawal reason, a withdrawal event time and an observation time, and the record is retained as a tombstone so that references from external observations and deviation decisions do not dangle.

A condition referenced by any external evaluation result or deviation decision may never be purged while that reference is live; purging requires prior confirmation from the referencing system that the reference has been released.

Retention periods, legal holds and physical erasure of this model's records are set and executed by the adopting Dimension's records-retention policy and by the referenced authority model for decision records; this model owns only the withdrawal marker, the disposition reference and the tombstone recording that a condition once existed.
Deleting a completeness assertion is prohibited; it is superseded instead, because removing it would silently return the scope to the open-world default and change the meaning of absence.

access.default_rule: Read access to condition declarations follows the access classification of the host subject: a condition is never more open than the least open of its two endpoints, and no consumer receives a condition stripped of its guard, lifecycle scope or completeness context. Write access is restricted to the condition steward for the relevant subject scope.
exceptions: A negative condition or an asserted contradiction may reveal the existence of an otherwise restricted prerequisite; where the prerequisite is restricted, the condition is disclosed in redacted form that preserves polarity and scope but withholds the endpoint identity.

Deviation bindings may be readable to a narrower audience than the condition itself where the referenced decision record is restricted by the authority model; in that case only the existence, type and validity window are disclosed.
Crosswalk and scale profiles are published at least as widely as any projection that cites them, since a projection is uninterpretable without its profile version.
Completeness assertions covering a restricted scope are disclosed as scope-limited statements without enumerating the restricted conditions themselves.
audit_requirements: Every creation, superseding revision and withdrawal of a condition records the acting identity, the event time and the observation time in RFC 3339 with explicit offsets.

Every ingested status snapshot and deviation binding records the external producer or decision reference; this model retains only its own write log and never claims custody of the producer's or authority's audit trail.
Refusals to project a guarded condition are logged with the target vocabulary and the specific distinction that could not be represented.
Access to redacted conditions and restricted deviation bindings is logged with the disclosure form applied.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md first and resolve Name and Type to confirm this is the Dependency / Impact condition mixin rather than a host subject model
Follow the Specification URL to load the scope statement, boundary notes and out-of-scope list before authoring or interpreting any condition
Follow the Storage type URL to learn the projection in use, remembering that the projection never alters the canonical direction, guard or completeness semantics
Follow the Interface URL to discover the read, create, update and delete operations and their preconditions
Follow the Processes URL for crosswalk profile versions, normalization rules, projection refusal rules and the deviation and completeness assertion procedures
Load the referenced crosswalk and strength scale profile versions last, and treat any condition citing an unresolvable profile version as unverifiable

coverage.claim: This pass covers the declaration surface and epistemic state of dependency conditions for WM-XCT-037: canonical direction, typed kind and lifecycle scope, obligation level and optionality encoding, ordered prerequisites, alternatives with cardinality thresholds, guards with skip-versus-fail semantics, comparison predicates and ranges, negative and contradictory conditions, and the separation of declared conditions from observed satisfaction, violation, deviation, unknown state and completeness. Every structural node is grounded in at least one primary source; impact propagation, resolution, evaluation and enforcement are deliberately excluded.

checklist.notes: A condition is a first-class addressable assertion, consistent with SPDX modelling a relationship as its own element and CycloneDX addressing endpoints by bom-ref. Identity priority places the authoritative master-system identifier first and forbids date-derived keys.

Two lifecycles are separated: the applicability scope of the condition (SPDX lifecycle scope: build, design, development, runtime, test, other) and the record lifecycle of the declaration (authored, superseded, withdrawn as tombstone). The lifecycle of the endpoints belongs to the host model.

Canonical dependent-to-prerequisite direction is fixed from SPDX from-to and CycloneDX ref-to-dependsOn, with explicit normalization of prerequisite-side forms such as Debian Enhances and RPM Supplements. Ordering and existence are kept as orthogonal axes per systemd.

Lifecycle scope, gated stage boundaries, guard evaluation timing (bounded versus continuous, per the Kubernetes ignored-during-execution scoping) and separate event and observation timestamps are all modelled. General effective-from and effective-until validity windows for a declaration itself have weaker primary support and are carried only for deviations.

Native term, source vocabulary and version, crosswalk profile version, normalizing actor, evaluator identity and issuing actor for completeness assertions are all recorded. Unmapped terms are retained as residue rather than coerced.

Roles define stewardship of conditions, vocabularies, observations and deviations, and a boundary reviewer guards against importing external semantics. The registry entry names no concrete maintainer, which is recorded as an omission for the adopting Dimension to close.

Following SHACL, declared constraints and validation results are separated, conformance is defined by an external processor, and severity is a result qualifier rather than an obligation level. This model records results by reference and performs no validation.

Access is bounded by the least open endpoint, with redaction rules for negative conditions that would otherwise reveal a restricted prerequisite, and narrower disclosure for restricted deviation bindings. The specific classification scheme is dimension-owned and has no external standard cited.

Conditions are withdrawn as tombstones rather than purged, purging is blocked while external observations or deviation decisions reference them, completeness assertions may only be superseded, and execution of retention, legal hold and erasure is explicitly owned by the adopting Dimension's records policy and the referenced authority model.

Crosswalks to SPDX, ECMA-424 CycloneDX, Debian Policy, RPM boolean dependencies, TOSCA requirements and Kubernetes affinity are declared as alignments with fidelity classification, and projection emits a lossiness report and may refuse rather than flatten.

Obligation level, optionality encoding (relationship type, distinct field or zero cardinality lower bound), preference weight with a named scale, and the RFC 2119 admission of justified departure are modelled, with an explicit refusal to assert a total order across incommensurable scales.

Guards, unmet-guard outcome (inapplicable versus failure, from the systemd condition-versus-assertion distinction), evaluation timing and an explicit prohibition on unconditional projection are modelled, grounded in RPM boolean operators and Debian architecture and build-profile restrictions.

Polarity, exclusion subtype, symmetry and asserted contradictions are first-class, grounded in Debian Conflicts and Breaks, RPM Conflicts with boolean expressions, systemd Conflicts and Kubernetes NotIn and DoesNotExist. Detection and resolution of conflicts remain external.

The open-world default is taken from OWL 2, the complete, incomplete and noAssertion values from SPDX, and the explicit empty declaration and opacity rule from CycloneDX. Negation basis distinguishes asserted absence from absence of evidence.

Predicate operators, half-open interval semantics and ordering-scheme dependence come from OSV and Debian version relations; quantitative thresholds carry unit, precision and measurement basis, and the ordering scheme itself is referenced, not defined here.

Project-schedule precedence types (finish-to-start, start-to-start, finish-to-finish, start-to-finish) and lead and lag semantics could not be verified against a retrievable primary source in this pass, so no such structure is asserted. Ordering is grounded only in systemd and Debian staged-installation evidence.

No authority defines a total order across an ordinal package-field grade, a three-level requirement-keyword scale and a cardinal scheduling weight. The model records the encodings and explicitly forbids cross-scale comparison rather than inventing a unifying scale.

Dependency conditions carry no intrinsic geometry. Where a condition is restricted by placement, that restriction appears as a guard variable such as a topology or region label and is modelled as an ordinary guard, not as spatial semantics.

The registry supplies an empty relations ledger and a review state of boundary-review-required, so all composition links here are candidates awaiting ledger confirmation. They are written to be non-owning by construction, but they have not been validated against a populated ledger.

known_omissions: Impact propagation, blast radius, criticality scoring and downstream effect, which belong to the impact split of WM-XCT-037 and are referenced only through boundary notes.
Transitive closure, cycle detection, shortest-path attribution and any other graph analytics over sets of conditions.
Resolution and solver behaviour: selection among alternatives, backtracking, preference application and dangling-requirement fulfilment.
Discovery and inference of undeclared conditions from artefacts, telemetry or code analysis, including confidence models for inferred edges.
Project-schedule precedence typology and lead and lag calculus, excluded because the candidate public-authority sources could not be retrieved in usable form during this pass.
A concrete named owner and maintainer for the vocabulary and profiles, which the registry leaves as designated by the adopting Dimension.
Quantitative risk or cost weighting of unmet conditions, which requires the impact split and an external scoring model.
Localisation and multilingual presentation of condition descriptions and consequence notes.
conflicts: Where strength lives differs by authority: SPDX encodes optionality as a distinct relationship type, Debian and RPM as distinct field names with graded meaning, TOSCA as a cardinality lower bound of zero, and Kubernetes as a required-versus-preferred flag with a numeric weight. No single encoding can round-trip all four without annotation.

CycloneDX dependsOn carries no strength axis at all, so projecting an optional or recommended condition into a CycloneDX dependency edge either loses the distinction or misrepresents it as mandatory; the model requires a lossiness report or refusal rather than a silent choice.

Direction is not uniform: Debian Enhances and RPM Supplements and Enhances are declared by the prerequisite side, and older SPDX vocabularies used inverse relationship names, so ingest must invert while retaining the native term.

Default epistemics conflict: CycloneDX states that absence from the graph is opaque and requires an explicit empty element to assert no dependencies, SPDX offers an explicit noAssertion value, while package archives are conventionally interpreted closed-world within a resolution context. The model adopts the open-world default and records the divergence.

Grammar expressiveness conflicts: RPM forbids combining if with or and unless with and, whereas Kubernetes match expressions and SHACL constraint components permit different nesting, so a neutral expression that is valid here may be unprojectable into RPM.

Ordering and existence are orthogonal in systemd but deliberately coupled in Debian Pre-Depends, which conflates a strength grade with a staged ordering guarantee; the model records both axes separately and preserves the native coupling as provenance.

Severity scales are not obligation scales: the SHACL Violation, Warning and Info scale qualifies results, while Debian field grades and RFC 2119 keywords qualify requirements. Conflating them would misreport a warning-severity result on an absolute requirement as a weak condition.
regional_assumptions: The evidence base is drawn from software supply-chain, packaging, orchestration and semantic-web standards published in English by international bodies; domain vocabularies in engineering, construction, clinical and regulatory settings may carry dependency notions this pass has not tested.

Retention periods, legal holds and the admissibility of a waiver or concession are jurisdiction-specific and are deliberately delegated to the adopting Dimension's records and authority models rather than fixed here.

Guards that encode export control, sanctions, licence acceptance or data-residency restrictions will be region-specific in practice; the model treats them as ordinary guard variables and makes no assumption about which jurisdictions apply.
Time handling assumes RFC 3339 offsets are available from source systems; where a source supplies only local civil time, ingest must reject rather than assume a regional offset.
adversarial_checks: Flattening test: take a condition guarded by an architecture restriction and a build profile, project it into a target vocabulary without guard support, and confirm the projection is refused or emits a lossiness report naming the dropped guard, never an unconditional edge.

Silence test: query a subject with no declared conditions and confirm the response returns an open-world marker or an explicit empty declaration, and never reports the subject as dependency-free by inference.

Inversion test: ingest a prerequisite-side declaration such as an Enhances or Supplements field and confirm the stored record is in canonical dependent-to-prerequisite direction with the native term retained in the normalization record.

Boundary-creep test: search every finding and function for any field that would evaluate a predicate, select among alternatives, decide an approval, gate an operation or retain an evaluator's report, and confirm each such concept resolves to a REFERENCE link, an out-of-scope entry or a boundary note instead.
Commensurability test: attempt to rank a Debian Recommends against a Kubernetes preferred rule with weight 100 and confirm the model refuses the comparison rather than producing an order.

Status-collapse test: ingest an evaluation result in which a guard was false and confirm the recorded status is not-applicable rather than satisfied, and ingest a case with no result at all and confirm the status is unknown rather than absent-and-therefore-satisfied.

Tombstone test: withdraw a condition that is referenced by a live external deviation decision and confirm the record survives as a tombstone, the reference does not dangle, and the model defers erasure to the adopting Dimension's retention policy.

Identity test: inspect every local identifier for a date-like component and every artifact identity strategy for use of an issue date as a key, and confirm the authoritative master-system identifier is preferred over any governed IRI or assigned UUID or ULID.
